title: Cyrus and the Hollow
premise: August Dravenmoor, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics he carves, keeps the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled memories, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy book, he learns he is the 'Hollow Bearer' foretold to carry a secret that could reignite the war between the living and the dead. Hunted by guild rivals and the revenant court alike, August discovers the secret is his own erased identity: he was once the war's last casualty, remade as a man with no past. In the end, August chooses to speak the truth aloud, dissolving himself into memory rather than let either side weaponize it—and the long winter breaks over a world that finally remembers him.
about_author: O. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed heirlooms in a northern port city. They write quiet, eerie fantasies about people who keep records of things better left forgotten.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: August carves a relic for a grieving widow and hears her dead son's last words, then files the transaction in the Hollow Guild's ledgers. His POV establishes his careful invisibility and his rule: never listen twice. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence—he serves grief but permits himself none.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Dust
chapters.summary: Auditing the prophecy vault, August finds today's date circled in a book a century old, beside the words 'the Hollow Bearer opens.' His POV; dread creeps under his routine. The beat is vertigo—the invisible man discovering he was always on the page.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: The widow returns, claiming her son spoke August's true name—a name August doesn't recognize. Guild mistress Vessa Corvane warns him to stop asking questions. His POV, paranoia mounting. The beat: the first crack in his certainty that he has no past worth hiding.

chapters.title: The Revenant Court Sends Regards
chapters.summary: An emissary of the dead arrives at the guild offering to buy the prophecy page outright. August refuses, then secretly copies it. Alternating POV with the emissary reveals both sides fear what August might remember. The beat: hunted from two directions, he chooses curiosity over safety.

chapters.title: Bone Remembers
chapters.summary: Carving a commission from pre-war bone, August hears fragments of his own voice in the relic's echoes—arguing, pleading, dying. Vessa catches him mid-vision and confesses the guild made him: wiped, remade, employed. His POV; betrayal and strange relief. The beat: identity as something done to him.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: The first snow carries whispers; the dead grow restless citywide as the prophecy date nears. Rival guilds and revenants converge on August. Told partly from Vessa's POV, we see her guilt and her plan to sell him to whichever side pays. The beat: the protectors were wardens all along.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Hollow City
chapters.summary: August flees into the undercity where the war's ruins still hum, guided by the widow's son's echo. He recovers a cache containing his own carved hand-bone, inscribed with the secret: the terms of the old armistice, written in his blood. His POV. The beat: terror transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of the Secret
chapters.summary: Cornered by the emissary, August learns the truth fully: he brokered the armistice, and both courts erased him because the terms require a living witness to renew them—or void them. Speaking them could end the stalemate or restart everything. Dual POV. The beat: power offered, corruption anticipated.

chapters.title: Where the Dead Keep Court
chapters.summary: August stands before the revenant court and the guild's assembled masters, both demanding the secret for themselves. Vessa betrays him; the emissary turns on its own court. August begins speaking the terms aloud as snow buries the hall. Climax; his POV. The beat: choosing truth over survival.

chapters.title: Remembered Into Spring
chapters.summary: Speaking the secret unmakes August's false self; he scatters into shared memory, heard now by every carver, every mourner. The war stays buried; the winter breaks. Epilogue from the widow's POV: she carves his name into plain wood, and somewhere, faintly, someone answers. The beat: identity restored not as selfhood, but as being remembered.
